recurringPatterns.pattern: Concessive doublet: what a source establishes immediately cancelled by what it cannot, dozens of times per chapter
instances: Jebel Sahaba establishes a concentration of violent injury...; it cannot establish a general rate for all hunter-gatherers of the period.
The inscriptions establish that Sargon's court valued conquest... They do not independently verify every geographical reach

recurringPatterns.pattern: Identical chapter-closing paragraph: roll-call of the chapter's cases then 'the historical change lay in…'
instances: Jericho's wall indicates recognition of vulnerability...; Talheim's mass burial records...; Göbekli Tepe demonstrates...
Yuan administration in northern China translated Mongol movement into rule...; Mamluk resistance at Ayn Jalut...

recurringPatterns.pattern: Cross-chapter recapitulation of the same exhibits re-narrated at near-original length
instances: Earlier states had extracted grain, labour, and taxes for armies, as the ration tablets of Uruk and the Assyrian records of deportation show.
Guernica, bombed on 26 April 1937 by aircraft associated with the German Condor Legion...

recurringPatterns.pattern: Two-sided institutional antithesis as the resolution of nearly every section
instances: State power made some dangers less immediate for some people and made other forms of coercion more regular.
The same capacity that makes a homicide prosecution more regular can make mass coercion more coordinated.

recurringPatterns.pattern: Uniform paragraph architecture, no short paragraphs, no scene, no variation in tempo
instances: Preservation changes the apparent geography of violence...
Magazines placed supplies near a route of operations...

summary: Genuinely serious argument sustained with discipline; cost is monotony: one paragraph shape, one closing move, one figure; redundancy a real defect (sentence duplicated verbatim in ch7, ch5 double landing, exhibits re-narrated); three drafting seams (a paragraph quoting its own earlier sentence, passages discussing what chapters 12 and 14 will cover).
